summary.headline: Music Broadcast Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR 40.8 cr (from INR 54 cr) but operating EBITDA turned positive at INR 6.1 cr (15% margin) on cost cuts.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined to INR 40.8 crore from INR 54 crore a year earlier, as advertiser spend stayed subdued in certain categories. Cost restructuring and hub-based operations lifted operating EBITDA to INR 6.1 crore from negative INR 3.5 crore, with margin at 15%. Reported PAT was a loss of about INR 48 crore (the call also cited an adjusted loss of INR 47.4 crore), versus a loss of INR 38 crore a year earlier. For FY26, revenue fell to INR 174 crore from INR 234 crore, while operating EBITDA margin rose to 18% from 17%, and the reported PAT loss widened to INR 53 crore from INR 33.8 crore.

segments.name: FCT / NFCT (revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 FCT to NFCT split was 80-20. Non-FCT (events, activations, on-ground) is about 22% of revenue and management expects it to keep rising.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital contributes about 8% of revenue, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance given; management remains optimistic on gradual ad demand recovery supported by economic recovery, festive spending and local advertiser traction.
Management says most cost efficiencies are already actioned and visible from Q4 onward; further gains expected from technology in transmission and broadcast.
Non-FCT events and activations are green-lit only against a margin benchmark, with growth driven by margin rather than top line; Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets showing more traction than Tier 1.
Management is not planning to deploy the company's cash reserves currently; cash is being held.
capex_capacity: Operations moved to a hybrid model: all 39 stations are live to advertisers and listeners, with operations run from regional hub stations.
Headcount was 458 at end FY26, down about 20% YoY, following a Q2 restructuring that removed duplicate roles.
Q4 inventory utilisation was 70%, and Q4 volumes were flat YoY.
Company holds decent cash reserves; no M&A, JV or inorganic plan was confirmed in the call.
demand_pricing: Q4 effective rate was 107 versus 115 a year earlier, a decline of about 7%.
Industry volumes are degrowing at about 2% per the CFO; company volumes were flat YoY in Q4.
Market share reportedly reached about 17.5% across the 15 Airchec-monitored markets at year end, rising each quarter from Q2 to Q4.
Top 5 ad categories are real estate, finance, pharma, auto and jewellery; finance and pharma showed the highest growth.
Q4 saw 1,600 new clients (32% of clients new), and 6,600 new clients for FY26. Company client count is about 7,000 versus 15,680 for the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost decline, and what is the FY26 headcount trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Restructuring in Q2 removed duplicate roles, with savings visible in Q3 and Q4. Headcount was 458 at year end, down about 20% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp drop in other expenses in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: A hybrid model: all 39 stations are live, but operations are run from regional hub stations rather than each station separately.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q4 effective rate, volume growth, inventory utilisation and FCT/NFCT split?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective rate was 107 vs 115 last year. Volumes were flat YoY. Inventory utilisation was 70%. FCT/NFCT split was 80-20.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company deploying its cash, and is M&A or JV being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: No current plan to deploy cash; it is being held. No M&A or JV plan was specifically confirmed; the answer focused on integrated solutions and AI.

qa_highlights.question: How will non-FCT evolve over 3-5 years, and how does its profitability compare to core?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-FCT is about 22% of revenue and rising. Events are green-lit only if they meet a margin benchmark, with more traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

qa_highlights.question: Industry volumes are degrowing about 2% while company volumes are flat. Why is market share stuck at 16.5-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market share has grown each quarter from Q2 to Q4, ending FY26 at about 17.5% across the 15 Airchec-monitored markets.

risks_watch: Revenue remains under pressure: FY26 revenue down about 26% and Q4 down about 24% YoY amid cautious advertiser sentiment.
Reported PAT losses widened for both Q4 (INR 48 crore) and FY26 (INR 53 crore) despite the EBITDA improvement; finance costs and NCRPS interest are a drag.
Effective rate declined to 107 from 115 YoY; watch pricing discipline against weak volumes.
Cost takeout is largely done, so future margin expansion depends on revenue recovery and technology-led efficiency.
Watch whether non-FCT (22%) and digital (8%) grow fast enough to diversify the revenue mix.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on cost and margin progress but cautious on revenue, describing advertiser sentiment as cautious and the industry as soft. Answers on the non-FCT and M&A questions were general, and no numeric guidance was given.
key_quotes: While revenue performance continued to remain subdued due to softer industry conditions, our efforts towards optimizing expenses and enhancing operational efficiencies supported in improving our margins and profitability during the quarter.
So we are extremely focused on profitability. And therefore, we have a certain benchmark margin, basis which we green light these events and activation, right?
So we ended the year at about 17.5% of the 15 markets, which are monitored by air check.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management is only optimistic on gradual ad recovery, with no capacity additions, and Q4 revenue fell about 24% YoY (INR 40.8 cr vs 54 cr) while industry volumes degrow about 2%.
